issues.legal_issue: A municipal authority may amend a finalized property-tax assessment list after the year for which it was in force to include property that escaped assessment, with the amendment operating on the list for the year to which that list applied.
material_facts: A building was assessed to property tax for several years on the basis of rent received, but rent from a portion of its basement was alleged to have been omitted from the assessment lists.
After those lists had been finalized and the relevant years had passed, the municipal authority gave notice that it intended to amend the lists to include the omitted rent.
The High Court held that amendments could operate only prospectively, and the municipal authority appealed.
issues.conclusion: The municipal authority had power to amend the finalized lists, even after the relevant years had expired, and the amendments could correct the lists for the years to which they originally applied. That power is subject to the requirement that it be exercised within a reasonable time; the reasonableness of the timing was not at issue.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 66 and 67 of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911 must be read together: the tax in an authenticated list applies to the ensuing year subject to amendments duly made afterward, and the words “at any time” permit amendment after finalization and after the list’s operative year has expired. An amendment to a list operates for the year for which that list was in force, rather than only for the year following the amendment. The power is subject to reasonableness. Section 68A, added later, expressly limits the effective date of amendments for property already included but erroneously valued or assessed; its different wording and scope support the wider operation of amendments under section 67 for property omitted altogether. Punjab National Bank v. New Delhi Municipal Committee supports amendment after finalization, while Municipal Corporation of City of Hubli v. Subha Rao Hanumanatha Rao Prayag is inapplicable because it concerned a different statutory scheme.

rule.if: municipal_property_tax_assessment_proceeding and property_omitted_from_assessment_list and omission_discovered_after_list_expired and amendment_within_reasonable_time

predicates.municipal_property_tax_assessment_procee: The proceeding concerns the assessment of property to municipal tax.
predicates.property_omitted_from_assessment_list: The municipal authority omitted property, or an assessable part of it, from an assessment list.
predicates.omission_discovered_after_list_expired: The municipal authority discovered the omission after the assessment list’s operative year had ended.
predicates.amendment_within_reasonable_time: The municipal authority sought to amend the list within a reasonable time after the relevant circumstances arose or were discovered.

issues.definition: When property was omitted from a municipal property-tax assessment list and the omission was discovered after the list’s year ended, the list may still be amended for its original year if the amendment is made within a reasonable time.
